chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: Denying that he copied Fletcher's charts at Connie's Inn
summary: Told that Sandy Williams recalled sneaking afternoon copies of Fletcher's charts, Horace says he could simply have asked Fletcher and thinks Sandy was joking.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Here's something that might be interesting to talk about. Let's see. It's -- I'm not sure -- oh, yeah, this is November, 1930. It says, "Sandy Williams came to New York, permanently, to join this band. He recalled that the Dunbar was hired out to different clubs each night. If Fletcher was indeed cooperating with some of his special arrangements, meaning that he was providing some of his arrangements to you, which I think you did tell me that the first day. "If Fletcher was indeed cooperating with some of his special arrangements, it might have been -- it might not have been all voluntary. In late November, 1930, Fletcher's band went into Connie's Inn a few blocks down 7th Avenue, and Sandy recalls that he, Horace and Talcott Reeves would go down to Connie's in the afternoon and copy off Fletcher's
charts onto their own manuscript paper. Of course, they would never those borrowed arrangements when Fletcher himself was listening." Do you have any comment about that?
I don't recall this, truthfully, because I, number one, I wouldn't have had to do it. All I had to do was ask for it.
Yeah, that's what really seemed strange to me when I read it.

Because why would he have given me anything I wanted before this and always did? I wouldn't have to do that. Or either I'd tell him if I was going to do it. I wouldn't have to slip, so I don't know where this information came from.
Oh, I could see you -- let's see. It was who that said this?
Sandy must have -- you know, Sandy was another one of those guys like Coleman Hawkins, you know, that was in that band.
He liked to play games, yeah.
So I think Sandy was putting somebody on.
Could have been, easily, because you could see where that could grow out of somebody just joking about it.
But what would we have done with something like that, you know, just a few parts? No way. I don't buy that.
